log.msg: Sources found: lew42com/public/fly/ (three.js flight sim, unpkg import, needs spaceship.glb) and lew42com/public/test/3D-scroll/page.js (perspective + scroll-driven perspective-origin + mousemove rotate + per-element translateZ).

Defect in the source 3D-scroll demo: perspective-origin is pinned to the scene box and swept 0%→200% on scroll, so on a 4000px page the vanishing point sits ~2000px away and translateZ(200px) at perspective 1200 displaces a layer ~400px. Port pins the vanishing point to the reading centre and counter-scales each layer by (P−z)/P so apparent size never changes with depth — that is what makes it subtle.

BUG FOUND BY PROBE, fixed: ext/depth never set --depth-focus on load. depth() runs inside content(), so the page is still unmarked and display:none for the microtask AND the first rAF; both measures bailed on !offsetParent and nothing retried, leaving base/middle at 0 and the vanishing point half a viewport off forever. Replaced the one-shot with a ResizeObserver on the scene. Verified: focus 450px at load on a 900px viewport, moves exactly 900 on a 900 scroll.

BUG FOUND BY PROBE (Mike reported the symptom), fixed: on a phone viewport the fly canvas measured buffer 2065x4207 with a client box of 412x1603 on an 839px-tall viewport. resize() ran once before device metrics settled and wrote setSize(787,1603) inline; no resize event ever fired for the settle; framework.css:25 `img,picture,video,canvas,svg,audio,iframe { max-width: 100% }` then clamped the WIDTH only, leaving the tall inline height. Result: horizontally squished view whose centre sat 801px down, i.e. the plane below the joystick. Two fixes: `canvas { position: fixed; inset: 0; max-width: none }` and a ResizeObserver on documentElement instead of the resize event. Not an is.mobile() difference and not an emulator artifact - the desktop-UA 390x844 run reproduced it identically.

Same class as the documented LayoutTool iframe clamp (`iframe { max-width: 100% }` made a 3440 frame measure 1920). framework.css line 25 has now bitten two modules; worth considering :where() around that reset.

Joystick knob was 50px low: framework.css puts `:first-child { margin-top: 0 }` in @layer util, the HIGHEST layer, which killed the knob's centring margin-top:-50px while margin-left survived. Re-centred with grid place-items instead of negative margins - immune by construction. Ring is now sized in vh (min(300px,26vh), bottom 4vh) so its top is always at 70% and clears the ship's fixed ~63-65%; the media query it replaced could only be right at one window size. Directions moved to the TOP of the screen, white on 50% black: the ship, the ring and the directions all want the lower half, and at 700px tall the band between ship and directions is 167px while the ring is 182px.

Verified at 1600 across /, /resume/, /framework/ext/, /framework/ext/depth/ and its api/ + files/ tabs: zero md-error boxes, zero 'Not written yet', zero horizontal overflow, no console errors. /resume/ measured clean at 400/1280/1920/3440. log.msg: Resume revision on Mike's notes. (1) No sidebar existed - the DOM has home's but visibleSidebars was 0, because the root page hides itself the moment you leave it. Left it that way: a resume is a document, not a docs section. (2) Centring needed a different lever than expected: .standard is a GRID whose main TRACK is --measure while the page stays full width and flush left, so --measure: 46em was sizing a track and centring nothing. Dropped .standard for a plain flow column with max-width + margin-inline: auto. (3) The page is now the one large card (.surface on .page-resume) AND the scene, so it is the plane everything moves against. (4) Four nested tiers, all verified composing with live preserve-3d: header 3 (+name 2 = 5), section 2 (+h2 2 = 4), job sub-card 1 = 3, page 0.

Anchor fix, Mike's diagnosis confirmed by measurement: framework.css scopes links to `:where(p, li, td, th, dd, blockquote, .md) a` deliberately, so that nav anchors (sidebar, tabs, toc, crumbs, preview cards) opt out by default and :visited cannot grey out the nav as you browse. The header contact links were bare `a` in a `div` and measured rgb(0,0,238) - raw UA blue. Moved into a `p`; they now measure rgb(63,63,63) ink with an rgb(255,143,96) orange underline.

LEAN was a module constant; promoted to the --depth-lean token (default raised 80 -> 120), read ONCE at wire time because a getComputedStyle per pointermove is a style flush per pointermove. Measured why it mattered: at 120 the horizontal separation between an h2 and the copy under it was 2.4px, invisible. /resume/ sets --depth-lean: 180 and the same measurement is 11.5px, with four distinct travel rates across the four tiers (page 0, section -10.4, job -16.1, h2 -21.9).

Depth slider max raised 2 -> 5. That is a hard ceiling, not taste: z is depth*step*scale and a layer at z >= perspective is behind the camera, where the counter-scale goes negative and the layer inverts. Verified at max: deepest layer scale 0.771, not inverted. Documented in the readme's tuning section. Also caught: `.pad` lives in @layer util and would have out-ranked `.page { padding: var(--page-pad) }`, making the page's own token dead - the page card takes .surface only.

Second resume revision, Mike's four notes. THE CORE FINDING: growth and drift are the same number. Perspective magnifies by P/(P-z) and displaces by d*z/(P-z) - one factor, not two - so 'reduce the perspective so it comes at you instead of running away' cannot work; lowering P raises both. The counter-scale was cancelling the growth and keeping ALL the displacement, i.e. exactly the wrong half. Added --depth-flatten (1 = cancel all growth, 0 = let it through) as the only lever that separates them, and documented the recipe: low flatten + low step + buy the motion back from the pointer, which costs no displacement.

Slider max 5 -> 3, and depth tiers re-cut from max composed 5 to max composed 3 (card 1 > section 2 > job 2.5 > heading 3). That is what fixed 'the h1 flies off the top': d in the displacement term is distance from the reading line, so every extra tier costs the most at the far end of a scrolled page. Measured at scroll 500: h1 drift at max slider is now 172px, and the name renders 24% LARGER rather than just leaving.

Rotation added, per LAYER not per scene: --depth-tilt rotates each card about its own centre. Rotating the scene is still forbidden (a rotateY about the middle of a 4000px box throws its far ends hundreds of px in z - the failure focus() exists to prevent); a single card is small enough that it costs nothing. JS now writes --depth-lean-nx/ny NORMALISED to -1..1 instead of px, so one value drives origin slide, tilt and shadow at three different scales without JS knowing any of them.

Mouse-following box-shadow works and is now built: it throws AGAINST the lean (light stays put, camera moves) and scales with the layer's own --depth-shadow. box-shadow is NOT on the list of properties that flatten preserve-3d. TRAP FOUND BY SCREENSHOT: --depth-shadow INHERITS, so a card setting 6px handed it to every heading inside it and headings cast card-shadows onto the card behind them - a pale box behind the text that looks like a background nobody wrote. Fixed by re-declaring --depth-shadow: 0px in the .depth-layer rule so each layer resets. Same class of bug: tilt COMPOUNDS through preserve-3d - three tiers at 2.5deg turned the innermost card 7.5deg and trapezoided it. Budget is deepest*tilt < ~3deg; resume runs 1deg.

Structure: the page is now the SCENE ONLY (no background) with gutter padding, and the sheet is a .resume-card layer inside it - a scene never transforms, so the page-as-card was the one flat thing on a page about depth. Three-tier background ladder built from color-mix off --surface/--ink so it inverts in dark mode, running the same way as the depth (lighter is closer, the theme's own rule): card grey 0.925, section near-white 0.977, job white.

NOT MINE, for whoever owns the DesignTool rename: /framework/ext/ and every page under it now 404s on /framework/ext/LayoutTool/widths/page.js. DesignTool/page.js declares `widths` in children: and files: but the dir has no page.js. Classic declared-child-without-page.js trap. My files reference LayoutTool nowhere.

Motion slider added — depth() now builds TWO knobs, and they are genuinely different. Depth (--depth-scale) is how far apart the layers sit; it buys growth and scroll parallax together because those are the same z/(P-z) factor. Motion (--depth-motion) is how hard the page REACTS: it multiplies lean, tilt and shadow throw in CSS, and the vanishing point's scroll travel in JS. Measured live at scrollTop 600: origin x 481/691/901/1110 and focus 1075/1075/1675/2275 across motion 0/1/2/3.

Two bugs found while building it. (1) Motion reached the pointer instantly (CSS reads the property) but the scroll parallax only caught up on the NEXT scroll event, so dragging the slider without moving looked like a dead control — focus() now returns its update and the slider calls it. (2) Motion's scroll gain is clamped to >= 1: gain 1 is exact tracking (displacement ~0 at the reading line) and anything under 1 makes the origin LAG the reading line, producing MORE drift, not less — the one setting where the slider would fight its own label. Below 1 it calms the pointer only.

CLAUDE.md trap hit for real: a formatter stripped the `@layer base, theme, site, util;` statement out of BOTH depth.css and resume.css, leaving each file opening on a bare `@layer theme {` / `@layer site {`. Nothing broke loudly, which is the entire point of that trap. Restored in both, with a comment naming the incident so the next reader knows it can happen.

Spacing pass on Mike's note: padding moved onto the three card tiers rather than the body — card clamp(1.5em,4%,3em), section clamp(1.5em,4%,2.75em), job clamp(1.25em,3.5%,2.25em); --flow 2.75em between sections; li margin-block-end 0.5em (last one zeroed by :last-child in @layer util); measure 58em -> 64em. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, for Mike: body copy now runs ~95 characters a line. The layout skill's ideal is ~75 and it flags >85. 60em would land near 89, 56em near 83. Mike asked for wider explicitly, so it ships at 64em and the number is the finding, not the page.

Docs re-synced: two claims had gone stale against the code — the readme still said per-layer rotation 'is not built' (it shipped the same day) and both readme and page.js still said the counter-scale 'cancels it exactly' (now governed by --depth-flatten, which /resume/ runs at 0.25). Tuning table now carries all eight tokens. Verified clean at 1600 across /, /resume/, /framework/ext/ and depth's overview/api/files tabs.

Depth slider: min 0.75, max 5, per Mike. The floor is a REAL trap, now reproduced and understood: below ~0.75 the layers are nearly coplanar, and a TILTED plane that is nearly coplanar with its parent intersects it INSIDE the card's own extent — preserve-3d then splits the geometry along the intersection line and interleaves the halves, so a card renders sliced down a hard diagonal with half of it behind its own parent. Screenshot at scale 0.1 + motion 3 + pointer in the corner reproduces it exactly. More z separation moves the intersection outside the card, which is why 0.75 works.

Mike asked why every section's --depth is 'locked at 1'. It is not a bug and the slider does reach them: --depth is the DECLARED tier, --depth-scale is the multiplier, --depth-z is the product. Measured: card z 22.5/30/90/150 and job z 11.3/15/45/75 at scale 0.75/1/3/5. What he was actually seeing is that the slider was capped at max 3, so dragging past it did nothing — at scale 5 the old build still reported z 90, identical to scale 3. Raising the max fixed the symptom.

Mike asked if motion was skewing. YES, and it was measurable. rotateY(a) then rotateX(b) composes to a 2D block [[cos a, sin a sin b],[0, cos b]] — that off-diagonal term is a genuine ROLL (in-plane rotation) and it compounds through every nested tier. Measured through /resume/'s three tiers: 0.025 / 0.101 / 0.228 deg of roll at motion 1/2/3 = 3.6px of skew across a 900px card. Replaced with ONE rotate3d about the axis perpendicular to the lean, (-ny, nx, 0), which gives a symmetric 2D block (pure stretch). Re-measured: roll exactly 0.000 at every motion level. Degenerate zero-length axis at pointer-centre verified safe — angle is 0 there and translateZ/scale both survive. NOTE: my first shear metric (column-vector dot product) was the wrong statistic; it counts legitimate 3D foreshortening, and reported 19px where the true roll-induced skew was 3.6px.

Value readouts added to both sliders (.depth-slider-value, tabular-nums, 2.6em floor so the row does not jitter while dragging), applied once at wire time because a slider whose min is above 0 cannot assume the page's token matches its handle.

STOP-AND-REPORT, NOT MINE, REPO-WIDE: `@layer base, theme, site, util;` has been DELETED from 48 tracked stylesheets (git diff confirms), including core/Page/Page.css, public/styles.css, ext/toc/toc.css, ext/markdown/md.css and the lew42 theme — plus all three of my own untracked ones, three separate times. CLAUDE.md lists this as a trap that never throws: the first @layer statement in a document fixes the order and a name first seen later is appended at the END, so dropping the restatement silently sorts `site` past `util` across the whole site. Restored my three (fly.css, depth.css, resume.css) with a do-not-deduplicate note. Did NOT mass-restore the other 48: another session is actively writing those files (it renamed LayoutTool->DesignTool and added a framework.css link to fly/index.html this hour), so a 48-file sweep would collide mid-write. Mike's call.

TIER TABLE: --depth moved out of inline styles and into resume.css, one selector per tier — Mike's ask, and it required a change to the ext. View.prototype.depth(steps) now takes steps OPTIONALLY: passing a number writes an inline --depth that beats every class rule, so a page with a dozen layers could not retune 'all its headings' without editing a dozen call sites. Bare .depth() adds the class and lets CSS say how deep. /resume/ now declares all six tiers in CSS: card 2, section 1, head 0.5, job 0.5, h1/h2 1.

That change needed a second RESET, exactly like --depth-shadow: --depth INHERITS, so a card declaring 2 would hand 2 to every layer inside it with no rule of its own — silently, and compounding through preserve-3d. .depth-layer now re-declares --depth: 1. Verified: every layer reports inline='' and its own CSS-declared tier, and the Depth slider amplifies each by its own value — card 45/60/180/300 and head 11.3/15/45/75 at scale 0.75/1/3/5, i.e. the card exactly 2x the section and the header exactly half, which is what Mike asked for.

AUTO MARGINS DO NOT CENTRE AN INLINE-LEVEL BOX. `.resume-depth { width: fit-content; margin-inline: auto }` was completely inert because the ext ships .depth-ctrl as display:inline-flex — the panel measured gapLeft 0 / gapRight 498 and nothing warned. Overriding to display:flex centres it: 249/249. Worth remembering as a general trap, not a resume one.

Also: motion capped at 2 (was 3); padding raised on all three card tiers and NOT on the page (card 40.6px, section 37px, job 29.9px, page held at 30px); root card contrast raised from color-mix(surface 90%) to 78% — measured srgb 0.925 -> 0.834 against near-white sections at 0.992 and white job cards, so the ladder reads clearly. Docs re-synced: method page documents the optional argument, readme gained a --depth row and the tier-table pattern, css file doc gained the inheritance reset.
